switch_rule: Every entry names the ONE config key that switches its module ON and OFF, as {table, key, on, off}. 'table' is one of the four config tables (rails.config_tables.CONFIG_TABLE_NAMES: judges, knowledge_views, observe, toolkits); 'key' is a dotted path that starts with that table and names one of its entry keys, with '<phase>' as the placeholder for a program's phase because a module's admission is about the module and not about one program's phase names; 'off' is the table's null arm, which composes to the same config hash as the table being absent (core.config.drop_null_arms), which is what makes the OFF arm a twin of the pre-table baseline rather than a third cell identity. 'proof' names the test that composes both arms and asserts they differ in exactly that one key. A FIFTH class, 'run', covers a module that is one config key and has no table entry because it is per-run and the four tables are per-phase: 'key' is the FLAT config key the fragment carries, it must be on the closed allowlist rails.config_tables.RUN_LEVEL_SWITCH_KEYS, 'off' is the key absent or the driver's documented default, and the entry owes a 'falsifier' -- kind 'request-bytes-identical' plus the receipt that proved it -- whose MANIFEST.sha256 the check re-verifies. That falsifier is the whole licence for being outside the tables: a module that moves one byte of the request cannot produce one and belongs in a table. A SIXTH class, 'episode', covers a module that changes the per-run native-role-episode graph itself -- how many times a role runs, or how the Solver samples and aggregates -- rather than what a phase observes, is supplied with, is judged by or may call, and does not claim the 'run' class's zero-request-bytes licence either: 'key' is the literal dotted path the fragment carries under native_episode (not 'episode.<key>', exactly as a run-class key is not 'run.<key>'), drawn from the closed allowlist rails.config_tables.EPISODE_LEVEL_SWITCH_KEYS, and 'off' is that key's own null form (rails.config_tables.is_episode_null_arm) rather than one shared null token, because native_episode.roles.solver's historical shape and native_episode.review_loop's 'off' marker are not the same value. Where a module's OFF arm is, today, more than one native_episode leaf that shares no common dotted prefix (the review-loop pairing of max_revisions and the Reviewer/Planner max_iterations) and an optional marker field declares and validates the one-key view against those leaves, the entry's 'proof' test treats the leaves the marker derives from -- and any policy-id/max_contacts consequence of switching it -- as DERIVED, and shows the composed ON/OFF pair differing only in the marker once those derived keys are set aside, exactly as it shows for any other one-key module otherwise. A SEVENTH class, 'stores', covers a module that adds a whole named store to knowledge_stores (a store's own release/snapshot pins plus its own supply, never one entry of the knowledge_views table, which wraps a PHASE's material/supply and not a STORE): 'key' is 'knowledge_stores.<store_id>', 'off' is null -- the named store absent from the knowledge_stores mapping (rails.config_tables.is_stores_null_arm) -- and 'proof' must show the two committed fragments differing in exactly that one top-level knowledge_stores sub-block, once each fragment's own speech-feature identity ids and free-English 'what_this_is'/'what_the_<store>_store_is' prose are set aside as bookkeeping, exactly as the four tables' own proofs already set comparable bookkeeping aside. The 'stores' class has TWO arm forms and an entry DECLARES which one it is in, in the field 'switch.form'. Form one, the default (no 'form' field), is the NULL form just stated: OFF is the named store absent, which is the shape of a module that ADDS a store the comparator does not carry. Form two, 'repin' (added 2026-09-17 by Fable E9 for cell B4b's module M4b, docs/results/2026-09-17-slurp-b4b-slot-store-v2-verdict.md, section 'The harness-admission consequence'), is the shape of a module that REVISES a store the comparator ALREADY carries: such a module moves neither more nor less than that store's two pinned leaves, so its OFF arm is the incumbent's {release, snapshot} pins and its ON arm is the successor's, each pin an object of 'relpath' and 'sha256' and nothing else (rails.config_tables.is_stores_repin_arm). The two arms must DIFFER -- a re-pin that pins the same bytes twice switches nothing -- and every pin whose relpath resolves to a file in this repository is re-hashed by the check, while a pin that resolves to no such file is a SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR relpath, which this model-free check never opens and checks for shape alone. The form is declared and never inferred: an entry whose OFF arm is not the store's absence and which does not say 'repin' is REFUSED, because an OFF arm silently allowed to be anything at all is exactly the loosening the null form exists to prevent. The re-pin form also changes the question a default plan is asked: 'not the null arm' is not enough, the plan must pin exactly the ON arm's release and snapshot bytes, so a plan still carrying the incumbent's pins -- or carrying no such store -- has NOT armed the module. A re-pin entry's 'proof' shows the same one-key property the null form's does, on the two committed fragments, with the pinned store's own derived artifacts (the prepared phase-supply materialized from it) set aside as DERIVED beside the usual bookkeeping, exactly as the episode class's proof sets aside the leaves its marker derives from.
